name: btrfs_truncate_inode_items
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid write transaction handle, root is the subvolume root, control points to a struct btrfs_truncate_control whose ino, new_size and min_type are set (min_type is BTRFS_EXTENT_DATA_KEY whenever new_size != 0), and control->inode is non-NULL if control->clear_extent_range is set. Postcondition: control->last_size is first set to new_size and control->sub_bytes to 0. The function allocates a path (returns -ENOMEM if that fails) and walks the items of inode control->ino backwards from the highest key, using btrfs_search_slot, until it meets an item of another objectid, an item whose type is below min_type, or an EXTENT_DATA item whose last byte is below new_size. Items of a type above min_type, and EXTENT_DATA items starting at or after new_size, are deleted (batched through btrfs_del_items; for each deleted extent control->last_size becomes its key offset); a regular or prealloc extent that straddles new_size is shrunk in place to a sector-aligned length and the walk stops with last_size = new_size; an unencoded uncompressed inline extent that straddles new_size is truncated in place, while an encoded or compressed inline extent that would need truncating makes the walk stop with the positive return value BTRFS_NEED_TRUNCATE_BLOCK. control->extents_found is incremented per EXTENT_DATA item visited, control->sub_bytes accumulates the bytes removed, the file extent range is cleared via btrfs_inode_clear_file_extent_range when control->clear_extent_range is set, and for each deleted extent with a non-zero disk bytenr (unless control->skip_ref_updates) a data ref is dropped with btrfs_free_extent. Any pending batched deletion is flushed before returning when the result so far is >= 0, and if the final result is 0 and last_size > new_size it is clamped to new_size. Returns 0 on success, BTRFS_NEED_TRUNCATE_BLOCK (positive) in the encoded-inline case, -EAGAIN when, on a shareable root, more than 32MiB of extents were freed and the transaction should end or the delayed refs reservation could not be refilled without flushing, or a negative errno from btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_inode_clear_file_extent_range, btrfs_free_extent or btrfs_del_items (the last three also abort the transaction). The path is released and freed on every return.

name: cow_file_range
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode, [start, end] is a delalloc range whose data space is reserved and whose extent bits are locked by the caller, locked_folio is NULL or the locked folio covering the start of the range, done_offset is NULL or a valid pointer, flags is a combination of COW_FILE_RANGE_* flags, and the range length (aligned to sectorsize) does not exceed the filesystem total bytes. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (after the cleanup below) for a free-space inode. Unless COW_FILE_RANGE_NO_INLINE is set it first tries cow_file_range_inline: a result of 0 is returned as 1 (the range was written inline and the IO and cleanup are already done) and a negative result is returned unchanged, both jumping to done, which sets *done_offset = end when done_offset is non-NULL and returns. Otherwise it loops reserving extents with btrfs_reserve_extent and, for each reserved extent, locks the extent range, creates the io extent map and an ordered extent (with csum cloning for the data relocation root), advancing start; on the zoned -EAGAIN case it waits for a zone to finish and retries when still at the original start, otherwise with done_offset non-NULL it shortens end to start - 1 and ends the loop with 0, and with done_offset NULL it fails with -ENOSPC. After the loop it clears LOCKED and DELALLOC over [orig_start, end], applies PAGE_UNLOCK (unless COW_FILE_RANGE_KEEP_LOCKED) and PAGE_SET_ORDERED to the folios, and returns 0 through done (setting *done_offset = end if done_offset is non-NULL). On any failure after the setup (-EINVAL, a negative errno from btrfs_reserve_extent other than the handled -EAGAIN, from btrfs_create_io_em, btrfs_alloc_ordered_extent or btrfs_reloc_clone_csums) the function undoes the current extent (drops the extent map, frees the reserved extent and the block group reservation), cleans up ordered extents and ends writeback for the already processed part, clears the bits and unlocks the folios for the current and untouched parts, frees the data qgroup reservation for them, logs an error and returns the errno; in that error case *done_offset is not written, and mapping_set_error is called on the inode mapping when the processed part is non-empty and locked_folio is NULL.

name: run_delalloc_nocow
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode (not zoned unless it is the data relocation root), [start, end] is a delalloc range whose data space is reserved and whose extent bits are locked by the caller, and locked_folio is NULL or the locked folio covering the start of the range. Postcondition: the function allocates its own path (-ENOMEM if that fails) and walks the file extent items covering [start, end] in order; for each sub-range that can be written NOCOW (can_nocow_file_extent says yes and a nocow writer reference on the block group is obtained) it calls nocow_one_range, and every sub-range that cannot (holes, extents that must be COWed, ranges before a NOCOW extent, and the tail after the last extent) is handed to fallback_to_cow, with the NOCOW writer reference dropped after each use. On success it unlocks the folios (PAGE_UNLOCK only) of the whole range, frees the path and returns 0. On failure it returns a negative errno (from btrfs_lookup_file_extent, btrfs_next_leaf, can_nocow_file_extent, fallback_to_cow or nocow_one_range, -EUCLEAN for an invalid on-disk file extent type, or -ENOMEM) after cleanup: the part of the range already handled up to the failure point has its ordered extents cleaned up and its delalloc bits cleared with LOCKED, DELALLOC and writeback started and ended on its folios; a range already cleaned by the failing fallback_to_cow or nocow_one_range call is skipped; the remaining untouched part is locked in the io tree, has LOCKED, DELALLOC, DEFRAG and DO_ACCOUNTING cleared, its folios unlocked and writeback started and ended, and its data qgroup reservation freed; the path is freed and an error message is logged.

name: btrfs_split_delalloc_extent
prose: Precondition: the caller holds inode->io_tree.lock (lockdep-asserted), orig is a valid extent_state of that io tree and split is an offset inside it. Postcondition: if orig->state does not have EXTENT_DELALLOC set the function returns without any change. Otherwise, if orig covers more than fs_info->max_extent_size bytes and count_max_extents(whole size) >= count_max_extents(orig->end - split + 1) + count_max_extents(split - orig->start) (the split does not need an extra extent), it returns without any change. In every other case (orig is not larger than max_extent_size, or the two halves need more extents than the whole) it increments the inode's outstanding extents count by 1 via btrfs_mod_outstanding_extents while holding inode->lock, and releases that lock before returning. Returns nothing; no reference or memory is acquired.

name: btrfs_finish_one_ordered
prose: Precondition: ordered_extent is a valid ordered extent whose IO has completed (data written or failed) and not yet completed here; the caller owns one reference and the ordered tree owns another. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and a negative errno on failure; the possible errors are -EIO when BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR was already set, an error from btrfs_zone_finish_endio, from joining the transaction, from btrfs_insert_raid_extent, -EINVAL for a NOCOW ordered extent still linked on its csum list, or an error from btrfs_mark_extent_written, insert_ordered_extent_file_extent, btrfs_unpin_extent_cache, add_pending_csums or btrfs_update_inode_fallback. If the extent was truncated to length 0 it returns 0 without inserting anything. For a non-NOCOW extent it locks the range (EXTENT_LOCKED | EXTENT_FINISHING_ORDERED) before joining a transaction; once a transaction is joined, a failure aborts it (the early -EIO, zone-finish, truncated-to-zero and join-failure paths have no transaction to abort). On success the file extent item is inserted (or the prealloc extent is marked written), the extent cache is unpinned, the checksums are added and the inode is updated. In all cases the extent bits of the range (DEFRAG, plus LOCKED, FINISHING_ORDERED and DELALLOC_NEW where they apply) are cleared and the transaction, if any, is ended. When ret is non-zero or the extent was truncated: on failure BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR is set on the ordered extent (btrfs_mark_ordered_extent_error), the extent map range not written is dropped unless the inode is a free-space inode, and when (failure or nothing written) the file extent was not already inserted and the ordered extent is neither NOCOW nor PREALLOC, the reserved extent is returned to the allocator (discarded first if the discard=sync option is on and it failed) and the data qgroup reservation is freed. In every case, even on failure, the ordered extent is removed from the inode and root lists, remaining bio cs lists are cleaned, and both references (the tree's and the caller's) are dropped, so the caller must not use ordered_extent afterwards.

name: btrfs_cont_expand
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode, oldsize <= size, and the caller does not hold the io_tree lock on the range being expanded. Postcondition: first btrfs_truncate_block zeroes the tail of the block at oldsize; if it fails its error is returned immediately with no lock taken. If size <= ALIGN(oldsize, sectorsize) it then returns 0 without further work. Otherwise it locks the extent range [hole_start, block_end - 1] (hole_start = ALIGN(oldsize, sectorsize), block_end = ALIGN(size, sectorsize)) after flushing ordered extents, iterates over the extent maps returned by btrfs_get_extent from hole_start up to block_end, and for each non-prealloc extent calls maybe_insert_hole (a no-op returning 0 with the NO_HOLES feature), marks the file extent range with btrfs_inode_set_file_extent_range and installs a hole extent map (if allocating the hole extent map fails, that range of the extent map tree is dropped, the inode is flagged for a full sync, and the loop continues as if successful); prealloc extents only get their file extent range marked. The range lock is released and the last extent map reference put before returning. Returns 0 on success; a negative errno from btrfs_get_extent, maybe_insert_hole or btrfs_inode_set_file_extent_range stops the loop and is returned; an error from btrfs_replace_extent_map_range is only returned if it occurs on the last iteration, because later calls overwrite the return value.

name: btrfs_invalidate_folio
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the lock on folio (so no new ordered extent or bio can be created for it) and offset and length describe the part of the folio being invalidated. Postcondition: returns nothing. It first waits for writeback of the folio and for the subpage spinlock. If the range is not the whole folio (offset != 0 or length != folio_size) it calls btrfs_release_folio(folio, GFP_NOFS), ignores the result and returns without touching extent state, ordered extents or qgroup data. Otherwise, unless the inode is being evicted (I_FREEING), it locks the extent range of the folio, then processes the folio range in segments: a segment not covered by any ordered extent has its qgroup data reservation freed and all extent state bits cleared; a segment covered by an ordered extent whose folio Ordered bit is still set has the Ordered bit cleared, DELALLOC, LOCKED, DO_ACCOUNTING and DEFRAG cleared in the io tree (not when evicting), the ordered extent marked truncated at that offset, and if btrfs_dec_test_ordered_pending reports that the ordered extent is complete, btrfs_finish_ordered_io is called and all extent state bits of the segment are cleared; a segment whose Ordered bit was already clear (endio already ran) leaves the ordered extent untouched. For every segment the ordered extent reference taken by the lookup is put, the qgroup data reservation of the segment is freed even when evicting, and (when not evicting) LOCKED, DELALLOC, DO_ACCOUNTING, DEFRAG (plus all bits where applicable) are cleared, which also unlocks the range. Finally the folio's checked bits are cleared, __btrfs_release_folio is called when the inode is not being evicted, and the folio's extent-mapped state is cleared. No lock or reference acquired is kept.

name: btrfs_prealloc_file_range
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode, mode is a fallocate mode mask, [start, start + num_bytes) is the range to preallocate with its data space already reserved, min_size is the minimum extent size, actual_len is the requested file length and alloc_hint points to a writable u64. Postcondition: this wrapper calls __btrfs_prealloc_file_range with no transaction handle, so each iteration starts and ends its own transaction. The loop reserves extents of at most 256MiB (at least min_size, and no larger than the previous allocation) with btrfs_reserve_extent, inserts a PREALLOC file extent item for each (insert_prealloc_file_extent), adds a prealloc extent map (if allocating it fails the range of the extent map tree is dropped and the inode is flagged for a full sync, without failing), sets BTRFS_INODE_PREALLOC, bumps iversion and ctime, extends i_size and disk i_size when FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE is not set and the new end exceeds both i_size and actual_len limits (to min(cur_offset, actual_len)), updates the inode, ends the transaction, and advances *alloc_hint to the end of the last extent. The result is the value of btrfs_update_inode of the last iteration: 0 when the whole range has been preallocated (or num_bytes is 0), a negative errno from btrfs_reserve_extent (for example -ENOSPC), from insert_prealloc_file_extent (the extent just reserved is freed), or from btrfs_update_inode (which also aborts the transaction and ends it) when a step fails. On failure only a prefix of the range has been preallocated; in every case, any part of the range not covered by a reserved extent has its reserved data space released with btrfs_free_reserved_data_space. No transaction remains open after return.

name: btrfs_do_encoded_write
prose: Precondition: iocb and from describe a write to a btrfs inode, encoded is a valid btrfs_ioctl_encoded_io_args, and the caller owns iocb, from and encoded. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, with nothing allocated and ki_pos unchanged, if the compression type is not ZLIB, ZSTD or an LZO size matching the filesystem sector size, if encryption is not NONE, the inode is NODATASUM, unencoded_len exceeds BTRFS_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED, the compressed byte count is 0, exceeds BTRFS_MAX_COMPRESSED or is not smaller than unencoded_len, or if the start (iocb->ki_pos), the end (unless the write reaches or passes i_size) or unencoded_offset is not sector aligned. Then it allocates and fills a folio array with the compressed data (-ENOMEM or -EFAULT on failure, freeing all folios), waits for ordered extents and invalidates the page cache over the range until no ordered extent or page remains, locks the extent range, and reserves data chunk space, qgroup data and delalloc metadata. It tries an inline extent first when the write is unencoded_len == len at offset 0; otherwise it reserves a disk extent, creates the io extent map and an ordered extent flagged ENCODED and COMPRESSED, extends i_size if the write passes it, unlocks the range, releases the delalloc extents and submits the compressed write (the folios are then owned by that IO). On success (both paths) it returns the compressed byte count orig_count (positive) and advances iocb->ki_pos by encoded->len; on the inline path the folios are put and freed here. On failure it returns the negative errno from btrfs_wait_ordered_range, invalidate_inode_pages2_range, btrfs_alloc_data_chunk_ondemand, btrfs_qgroup_reserve_data, btrfs_delalloc_reserve_metadata, __cow_file_range_inline, btrfs_reserve_extent, btrfs_create_io_em or btrfs_alloc_ordered_extent, with ki_pos unchanged, the extent range unlocked, the reserved extent freed and the extent map dropped when created, the delalloc, qgroup and data space reservations released, and all folios put and the array freed.

name: btrfs_ioctl_snap_destroy
prose: Precondition: file is a directory file on a btrfs mount, arg is a user pointer to a struct btrfs_ioctl_vol_args (destroy_v2 false) or btrfs_ioctl_vol_args_v2 (destroy_v2 true) naming the subvolume, either by NUL-terminated name or, for v2 with BTRFS_SUBVOL_SPEC_BY_ID, by a subvolid not below BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID. Postcondition: returns -EOPNOTSUPP (with an error message) on extent tree v2, -EOPNOTSUPP for unsupported v2 flags, and the error from memdup_user (-EFAULT or -ENOMEM) directly with nothing allocated. It then validates the name or id (-EINVAL for subvolid < BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID, a name containing '/' or equal to "..", or an invalid vol_args name; errors from btrfs_check_ioctl_vol_args*), takes write access on the mount (mnt_want_write_file), and for SPEC_BY_ID resolves the dentry and its parent (-EOPNOTSUPP on an idmapped mount when the parent differs from the directory the ioctl was called on). It then returns -ENOTDIR if the parent is not a directory, -EINTR if the killable wait for the parent's i_rwsem is interrupted, looks the name up (-ENOENT for a negative dentry), applies the permission checks for non-CAP_SYS_ADMIN callers (-EPERM without the user_subvol_rm_allowed option, -EINVAL if the ioctl was called on the subvolume itself, errors from inode_permission and btrfs_may_delete), returns -EINVAL if the inode is not a subvolume root (inode number BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID), and otherwise deletes the subvolume with btrfs_delete_subvolume while holding the subvolume inode lock, calling d_delete_notify on success. Returns 0 on success, otherwise the negative errno of the failing step; nothing is deleted on failure. On every path after the arguments were copied it releases what it acquired: the dentry reference, the parent directory lock if taken, the new parent dentry if one was allocated, the mount write reference, and the kernel copies of the arguments and the subvolume name.

name: btrfs_ioctl_subvol_sync
prose: Precondition: argp is a user pointer to a struct btrfs_ioctl_subvol_wait, readable always and writable for the modes that return data. The contents are validated by the function, not assumed. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if the argument cannot be copied from the user (and, for the data-returning modes, if copying back fails). Mode COUNT copies back the number of entries in fs_info->dead_roots and returns 0. Mode PEEK_FIRST copies back the id of the last entry of dead_roots (the one deleted first) or 0 if the list is empty, and PEEK_LAST the id of the first entry or 0, both returning 0. Mode WAIT_FOR_QUEUED sets subvolid to the id of the last entry of dead_roots (returning -ENOENT if the list is empty) and then behaves as WAIT_FOR_ONE, which returns -EINVAL for a subvolid in the open range (0, BTRFS_FIRST_FREE_OBJECTID) or above BTRFS_LAST_FREE_OBJECTID; any other mode returns -EINVAL. On a platform where unsigned long is narrower than u64 a subvolid above U32_MAX gives -EOVERFLOW. The wait loop then, under subvol_sem read lock (-EINTR if its interruptible acquisition is interrupted), looks the root up in fs_roots_radix: -ENOENT if it is absent, -EEXIST if its root refs are positive, and otherwise (refs not positive, i.e. dying) it sleeps one second interruptibly (-EINTR if woken early) and repeats. The branch that copies the structure back and returns 0 after waiting is taken only when refs reads as -1 for a root that is still found, which a found root does not normally have, so in practice a wait ends with -ENOENT, -EEXIST or -EINTR. No lock is held and no reference is kept on return.

name: btrfs_split_ordered_extent
prose: Precondition: ordered is a valid ordered extent that is not compressed, has disk_num_bytes == num_bytes, and is not partially completed (bytes_left is 0 or equal to disk_num_bytes), and 0 < len < ordered->num_bytes. Postcondition: returns ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) if len >= num_bytes, if the extent is partially completed or compressed in the sense above; returns ERR_PTR(BTRFS_FS_ERROR or -EIO) if BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR is set; returns the error of alloc_ordered_extent if allocation fails. Otherwise it creates a new ordered extent covering the first len bytes (same file_offset, disk_bytenr, flags and compress type), and, with the root's ordered_extent_lock and the inode's ordered_tree_lock held, trims the original so it covers only the remainder (file_offset, disk_bytenr, num_bytes, disk_num_bytes and ram_bytes advanced or reduced by len; bytes_left reduced by len, or the new one marked 0 when IO is already done; truncated_len split between the two when the original is truncated), moves the checksum entries covering the first len bytes to the new extent, inserts the new extent in the inode's ordered tree (panics if an extent already exists at that offset), adds it to the root's ordered_extents list and increments nr_ordered_extents. The new extent is returned with one extra reference for the tree on top of the creation reference; the original keeps its references and stays in the tree.

name: btrfs_quota_enable
prose: Precondition: the caller holds fs_info->subvol_sem for writing and not qgroup_ioctl_lock, and quota_ctl_args->cmd is the enable or simple-quota enable command. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (with an error message) on an extent tree v2 filesystem; returns 0 without changes if fs_info->quota_root is already set (including when another task set it while the lock was dropped). Otherwise it adds sysfs qgroup entries, starts a transaction on the tree root, creates the quota tree with a QGROUP_STATUS item, sets fs_info->qgroup_flags (ON plus SIMPLE_MODE and the SIMPLE_QUOTA incompat bit for simple quotas, or INCONSISTENT for full), adds a qgroup item and rb/sysfs entry for every subvolume found through ROOT_REF items and for the fs tree, records qgroup_enable_gen and BTRFS_FS_SQUOTA_ENABLING for simple mode, drops and retakes qgroup_ioctl_lock around the transaction commit, and after a successful commit publishes fs_info->quota_root and sets BTRFS_FS_QUOTA_ENABLED (clearing SQUOTA_ENABLING). In full mode it then initialises and queues a rescan (an -EINPROGRESS from the rescan init is ignored); simple mode skips the rescan. Returns 0 on success. On failure it returns the negative errno (-ENOMEM, or from btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups, btrfs_start_transaction, btrfs_create_tree, btrfs_insert_empty_item, btrfs_search_slot_for_read, btrfs_next_item, add_qgroup_item, btrfs_sysfs_add_one_qgroup or the commit), quota_root is not published, the transaction is aborted for most failures, the quota root reference taken is put, the sysfs qgroup entries are deleted, an un-committed transaction is ended, and if the commit itself fails in simple mode SQUOTA_ENABLING is cleared and qgroup_enable_gen reset to 0. qgroup_ioctl_lock is always released before returning.

name: btrfs_add_qgroup_relation
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle, prealloc is a non-NULL caller-allocated btrfs_qgroup_list whose ownership passes to the function (it is either linked into the rbtree or freed). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, freeing prealloc without taking qgroup_ioctl_lock, if btrfs_qgroup_level(src) >= btrfs_qgroup_level(dst). Otherwise it takes fs_info->qgroup_ioctl_lock and releases it before returning on every path. With no quota root it returns -ENOTCONN, if the src or dst qgroup is missing it returns -EINVAL, if the relation already exists -EEXIST (prealloc freed in each case). It then writes the relation items on disk in both directions (add_qgroup_relation_item; if the second write fails the first is deleted again, and the error is returned with prealloc freed), and under qgroup_lock links the relation into the rbtree with __add_relation_rb (a negative result is returned, prealloc already consumed) and updates the accounting with quick_update_accounting(src, dst, 1) (on failure the qgroups are marked inconsistent and its negative errno returned; the relation stays added), followed by squota_check_parent_usage. Returns 0 on success.

name: btrfs_qgroup_inherit
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle, objectid is the id of the new subvolume's qgroup, srcid is 0 or the id of the source qgroup, inode_rootid is the id of the containing root, and inherit is NULL or a valid btrfs_qgroup_inherit whose trailing array has at least num_qgroups + 2*num_ref_copies + 2*num_excl_copies entries (the entries are rewritten in place: invalid ids are zeroed). Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if quotas are not enabled. Otherwise it allocates a qgroup node (-ENOMEM if that fails), takes qgroup_ioctl_lock unless the transaction is already in TRANS_STATE_COMMIT_DOING, and returns -EINVAL if there is no quota root. In simple quota mode with inherit NULL it builds an automatic inherit with qgroup_auto_inherit (its error is returned; that inherit is freed at the end). It zeroes entries naming unknown qgroups or qgroups not of a higher level than objectid, creates the qgroup item for objectid, adds the relation items (ignoring -EEXIST) and preallocates the relation nodes, inserts the new qgroup in the rbtree with inherited limits if BTRFS_QGROUP_INHERIT_SET_LIMITS is set, in full mode copies counters and limits from the source qgroup (silently doing nothing more for an unknown srcid), links relations with add_relation_rb, runs qgroup_snapshot_quick_inherit per relation when srcid is set, and applies the ref and excl copy lists (-EINVAL if a listed qgroup is missing). On success it finally registers the qgroup in sysfs and returns 0. On error it returns the negative errno of the failing step (-EINVAL, -ENOMEM, or from qgroup_auto_inherit, add_qgroup_item, add_qgroup_relation_item, add_relation_rb, qgroup_snapshot_quick_inherit, btrfs_sysfs_add_one_qgroup), leaving the qgroup state partially updated. In all non-early-return cases the qgroups are marked inconsistent when a rescan is needed (source had parents with no inherit, quick inherit not possible, or counters tweaked by copy lists), qgroup_lock and qgroup_ioctl_lock (if taken) are released, and the preallocated nodes, the prealloc qgroup if unused and a self-allocated inherit are freed.

name: qgroup_rescan_leaf
prose: Precondition: trans and path are valid, path is not in use, and the caller does not hold fs_info->qgroup_rescan_lock. Postcondition: if full qgroup accounting is not active it returns 1 immediately, without taking the lock and leaving qgroup_rescan_progress unchanged. Otherwise it takes qgroup_rescan_lock and searches the extent root at fs_info->qgroup_rescan_progress with btrfs_search_slot_for_read. If that search returns non-zero (1 for no more items, or a negative errno) it sets the progress objectid to (u64)-1, releases the path, drops the lock and returns that value. Otherwise it records whether the path is on the last leaf, sets the progress objectid to the last key's objectid in the leaf plus 1, clones the leaf (on failure it drops the lock and returns -ENOMEM; the path is not released in this case), releases the path and the lock, and for every EXTENT_ITEM or METADATA_ITEM in the cloned leaf from the starting slot it finds all roots of the extent (btrfs_find_all_roots) and accounts the extent with btrfs_qgroup_account_extent (old roots NULL); the first negative errno from either stops the scan and is returned, with the progress left advanced. The cloned leaf is always freed. If it ends without error and the last leaf was reached it returns 1 and sets the progress objectid to (u64)-1, otherwise it returns 0 (more leaves remain).

name: btrfs_qgroup_rescan_worker
prose: Precondition: work is the qgroup_rescan_work member of a valid btrfs_fs_info; the function returns nothing. Postcondition: in simple quota mode it returns immediately without doing anything (completion is not signalled). Otherwise it allocates a path (on failure the error -ENOMEM is recorded and only the final status handling runs), sets it to search commit roots without locking, and loops while no error occurred and rescan_should_stop() is false: it starts a transaction on the fs root (the loop ends with the error if that fails), runs qgroup_rescan_leaf, and commits the transaction when the scan reports completion (result > 0) or just ends it. After the loop the path is freed; under qgroup_rescan_lock the INCONSISTENT flag is cleared if the scan completed (result > 0) while it was set, or set if the scan failed or was stopped. If any leaf was rescanned it then starts a transaction on the quota root (logging an error and recording it on failure). Under the lock again it clears the RESCAN flag unless the scan was merely paused (not cancelled), updates the qgroup status item if a transaction exists (an error is logged), sets qgroup_rescan_running to false, clears the CANCEL_RESCAN flag and signals qgroup_rescan_completion. If a transaction was started it is ended and a message is logged for paused, cancelled, completed or failed. The function releases all locks and its path before returning.

name: try_flush_qgroup
prose: Precondition: root is a btrfs root, the caller holds no transaction handle (current->journal_info is NULL, asserted); the function may sleep. Postcondition: if the caller does hold an open transaction (WARN_ON path) it returns 0 without doing anything. If BTRFS_ROOT_QGROUP_FLUSHING is already set by another task it waits until that bit is cleared and returns 0, without flushing or clearing the bit itself. Otherwise it sets the bit, starts delalloc writeback for the root (btrfs_start_delalloc_snapshot); if that fails it skips to cleanup with its negative errno, and otherwise waits for all ordered extents, runs and waits for the delayed iputs, and commits the current transaction, returning 0 or the error from btrfs_commit_current_transaction. On the paths where it set the bit (all but the two early returns) it clears BTRFS_ROOT_QGROUP_FLUSHING and wakes the waiters on root->qgroup_flush_wait before returning.

name: rmw_rbio
prose: Precondition: rbio is a valid btrfs_raid_bio queued for a read-modify-write and its stripe lock is held by the caller; the function returns nothing. Postcondition: rbio_orig_end_io(rbio, errno_to_blk_status(ret)) is called exactly once on every path, with ret 0 on success. It first allocates the parity pages; then, if the rbio is not a full-stripe write and some data sector lacks a page or is not uptodate, it allocates the data pages, indexes the pages and reads and recovers the stripe (rmw_read_wait_recover); a failure of any of these three steps ends the function with that negative errno before RBIO_RMW_LOCKED_BIT is set and before any write is built. Otherwise it sets RBIO_RMW_LOCKED_BIT under bio_list_lock, clears the error bitmap, indexes the pages, caches the pages when the rbio is not full (a full rbio clears RBIO_CACHE_READY_BIT), generates P/Q for every sector, assembles the write bios (a negative errno from rmw_assemble_write_bios ends the function with that errno, after the lock bit was already set), submits them, waits until stripes_pending drops to 0 and reports -EIO if any sector row has more errors than rbio->bioc->max_errors, otherwise 0.

name: btrfs_relocate_block_group
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem, group_start is the start of a block group and, for a data block group, the caller has started a superblock write section. Postcondition: it returns early, before taking any reference, with the non-zero result of wait_on_bit on BTRFS_FS_UNFINISHED_DROPS (interrupted wait), -EINTR if the filesystem is closing, -ENOENT if no block group starts at group_start, and, after taking the block group reference, -ETXTBSY if the block group is pinned by a swapfile or -ENOMEM if the reloc control cannot be allocated (the block group reference is put before these two returns). Otherwise it starts a reloc chunk, sets the block group read-only, deletes its free space cache inode, creates the data relocation inode, waits for block group reservations, nocow writers and ordered extents, finishes the zone, and repeatedly calls relocate_block_group under the cleaner mutex (after the first MOVE_DATA_EXTENTS stage that found file extents it waits for ordered extents, invalidates the inode's page cache and moves to UPDATE_DATA_PTRS) until no extents are found or an error occurs. It returns 0 on success, in which case the block group stays read-only, or the first negative errno (reloc_chunk_start, btrfs_inc_block_group_ro, -ENOMEM for the path, delete_block_group_cache other than -ENOENT, create_reloc_inode, relocate_block_group or btrfs_wait_ordered_range). On every return after the reloc control was allocated the block group reference is put and the reloc control is freed; if the reloc chunk start succeeded, the data inode is released (iput) and the reloc chunk ended, and on an error after the block group was made read-only the read-only count is dropped again (btrfs_dec_block_group_ro).

name: btrfs_recover_relocation
prose: Precondition: called while mounting a read-write btrfs filesystem to resume a relocation interrupted by a crash; fs_info->tree_root and fs_info->data_reloc_root are usable. Postcondition: it scans the tree root backwards for ROOT_ITEMs with objectid BTRFS_TREE_RELOC_OBJECTID, reads each as a reloc root and collects it; for a reloc root with root refs > 0 whose fs root no longer exists (-ENOENT) it zeroes the reloc root's refs via mark_garbage_root. If no reloc roots exist it skips the recovery. Otherwise it allocates a reloc control (-ENOMEM on failure), starts a reloc chunk, joins a transaction on the extent root, attaches each live reloc root to its fs root (roots whose refs are 0 are only queued for deletion), commits that transaction, merges the reloc roots with their fs roots (merge_reloc_roots), joins and commits another transaction, and cleans dirty subvolumes. On every path it frees the unprocessed reloc roots list, the path, the reloc control if allocated, releases recovered fs roots and ends the reloc chunk if started. If everything succeeded (ret == 0, which also holds when no reloc roots were found) it finally runs btrfs_orphan_cleanup on the data relocation root and returns its result. Returns 0 on success or a negative errno (-ENOMEM, or an error from btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_read_tree_root, btrfs_get_fs_root other than the -ENOENT case, mark_garbage_root, reloc_chunk_start, joining or committing a transaction, __add_reloc_root, clean_dirty_subvols when no earlier error, or btrfs_orphan_cleanup).

name: btrfs_reloc_cow_block
prose: Precondition: trans, root, buf and cow describe the COW of tree block buf into cow in transaction trans; when relocation is active and root is the reloc tree with create_reloc_tree set, the backref cache has a node at buf's level. Postcondition: returns 0 without any change if no relocation is active (fs_info->reloc_ctl is NULL). Otherwise the kernel BUGs if the stage is UPDATE_DATA_PTRS and root is the data relocation root; first_cow is true when buf's generation is not newer than root's last snapshot. When root is the tree reloc root and rc->create_reloc_tree is set: if the cached node's bytenr and new_bytenr both differ from buf->start it logs an error and returns -EUCLEAN with no change; otherwise it drops the node's old extent buffer, takes a reference on cow and stores it as node->eb with node->new_bytenr = cow->start, moves the node to the pending list for its level if it was not pending, calls mark_block_processed when first_cow, and adds buf->len to rc->nodes_relocated when first_cow and level > 0. In all cases that did not return -EUCLEAN, if buf is a leaf (level 0), first_cow is set and the stage is UPDATE_DATA_PTRS, it returns the result of replace_file_extents(trans, rc, root, cow) (0 or a negative errno); otherwise it returns 0.

name: btrfs_subvolume_reserve_metadata
prose: Precondition: root is a btrfs root, rsv is the block reservation to be charged, items is the number of metadata items to reserve space for, and use_global_rsv says whether the global reservation may be used as a fallback. Postcondition: if qgroups are enabled it first reserves 3 * nodesize of qgroup metadata prealloc space (one for the parent inode, two for the directory entries) and returns that function's non-zero error unchanged without any other effect. It then sets rsv->space_info to the metadata space info and adds the calculated insert-metadata size for items to rsv with flush-all reservation; if that fails with -ENOSPC and use_global_rsv is true it instead migrates that many bytes from the global block reservation. If the final result is an error and a qgroup reservation was made, the qgroup prealloc reservation is freed again and the error is returned. On success it adds the qgroup bytes to rsv->qgroup_rsv_reserved under rsv->lock and returns 0.

name: get_cur_inode_state
prose: Precondition: sctx is a valid send context with sctx->send_root set (sctx->parent_root may be NULL), ino and gen identify an inode, send_gen and parent_gen may be NULL. Postcondition: looks the inode up in the send root and, if present, in the parent root; an inode absent from a root or with nlink 0 there counts as not existing in it. If it exists in both roots, the result is inode_state_no_change when both generations equal gen, inode_state_did_create (ino < sctx->send_progress) or inode_state_will_create when only the send root generation equals gen, inode_state_did_delete or inode_state_will_delete (same test) when only the parent root generation equals gen, and -ENOENT when neither does. If it exists only in the send root, the result is did_create or will_create when its generation equals gen, otherwise -ENOENT; if it exists only in the parent root, did_delete or will_delete when its generation equals gen, otherwise -ENOENT; if in neither, -ENOENT. A negative errno other than -ENOENT from get_inode_info (send root first, then parent root) is returned unchanged. Side effects: if send_gen is non-NULL it is set (before the parent lookup) to the send root generation or 0 if the inode does not exist there; if parent_gen is non-NULL and parent_root is non-NULL it is set to the parent root generation or 0 if it does not exist there; neither is written when the send root lookup fails with an error, and parent_gen is never written when there is no parent root.

name: process_extent
prose: Precondition: sctx describes the current inode, path points at an EXTENT_DATA item whose key is key in the send root. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately, queuing nothing, if the current inode is a symlink. For an incremental send of an existing inode (parent_root set and not cur_inode_new) it calls is_extent_unchanged: a negative errno is returned; if the extent is unchanged it queues no data but still goes to maybe_send_hole (which may send a hole command and updates cur_inode_last_extent); if it changed it continues below. For a full send or a new inode, a PREALLOC extent, or a REG extent with disk bytenr 0 (a hole), returns 0 with nothing queued and without calling maybe_send_hole. Otherwise it calls find_extent_clone (a negative errno other than -ENOENT is returned; -ENOENT means no clone source), then send_write_or_clone (any non-zero result is returned), and finally returns the result of maybe_send_hole (0 or a negative errno), which may queue a hole command for the gap before this extent and sets cur_inode_last_extent to the end of this extent.

name: finish_inode_if_needed
prose: Precondition: sctx holds the state of the current inode (cur_ino and cur_inode_* fields), send_root is set, parent_root may be NULL. Postcondition: returns 0 at once, without anything else, if sctx->ignore_cur_inode is set. Otherwise process_recorded_refs_if_needed is called (a negative result goes to the exit), and send_progress becomes cur_ino + 1 if refs were processed and no move is pending. The function then jumps to the exit, queuing no chown, chmod, hole or truncate command, if cur_ino is 0, the current inode is deleted, or at_end is false and cmp_key->objectid == cur_ino. On the full path it reads the inode info from the send root (and the parent root for an incremental send of an existing inode) to decide need_chown, need_chmod, need_fileattr and need_truncate; for a regular file, when need_send_hole holds it refreshes cur_inode_last_extent with get_last_extent(sctx, (u64)-1) if that value is (u64)-1 or below cur_inode_size, and sends a hole up to cur_inode_size if the range is not already a hole in the parent; it then sends a truncate if need_truncate; it sends the needed chown, chmod, fileattr, the verity command (if the protocol supports it and the inode needs it) and capabilities; and if the current inode is not waiting for a move it applies the children directory moves, sets send_progress to cur_ino + 1 and issues the utimes command (cached for later if the inode is a non-empty directory). On every path other than the initial ignore_cur_inode return, if no error occurred so far, the result of trim_dir_utimes_cache is returned. A negative errno from any step is returned, possibly after some commands were queued.

name: changed_inode
prose: Precondition: sctx is an initialized send context whose cmp_key identifies the inode, left_path/right_path point at the inode items needed for result (NEW and CHANGED use left_path, DELETED and CHANGED use right_path), and result is a btrfs_compare_tree_result. Postcondition: first it closes the previous current inode (drops its page cache range if requested and iput) and resets cur_ino = cmp_key->objectid, cur_inode_new_gen = false, cur_inode_last_extent = (u64)-1, cur_inode_next_write_offset = 0, ignore_cur_inode = false, empties cur_inode_path and sets send_progress = cur_ino. Then for NEW: if the inode has nlink 0 it sets ignore_cur_inode and returns 0; otherwise it fills cur_inode_gen/new/deleted/size/mode/rdev from the send tree and, unless it is the root directory, calls send_create_inode_if_needed. For DELETED it fills gen, size and mode from the parent tree, marks the inode deleted and not new, and returns 0. For CHANGED: if both nlinks are 0 it ignores the inode and returns 0; cur_inode_new_gen is set when the generations differ (not for the root directory) or exactly one nlink is 0; in the new_gen case it processes the old inode as deleted (process_all_refs DELETED) when the old nlink is > 0, then, if the new nlink is > 0, as a new inode (send_create_inode_if_needed, process_all_refs NEW, send_progress = cur_ino + 1, process_all_extents, process_all_new_xattrs); otherwise it records the send-tree gen, size and mode with new and deleted false. Returns 0, or the negative errno of the first failing step, in which case the per-inode fields may be only partly updated.

name: btrfs_ioctl_send
prose: Precondition: send_root is a btrfs root, arg is the kernel copy of struct btrfs_ioctl_send_args (clone_sources is a user pointer), and the caller is the ioctl handler. Postcondition: returns -EPERM without any side effect if the caller lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN or the send root is dead or not read-only, and -EAGAIN if a dedupe is in progress on the send root; otherwise it increments send_root->send_in_progress and from then on all failures go through a common cleanup. It returns -EINVAL (too many clone sources, or the compressed flag with protocol version < 2), -EOPNOTSUPP (unknown flags), -EPROTO (version above BTRFS_SEND_STREAM_VERSION), -EBADF (send_fd not open for writing), -ENOMEM, -EFAULT (copying the clone source ids), errors from btrfs_get_fs_root for clone or parent roots, -EPERM for a clone or parent root that is not read-only or is dead, -EAGAIN for one with a dedupe in progress, and errors from flush_delalloc_roots, ensure_commit_roots_uptodate, send_subvol, send_utimes (for the cached directory times) and the begin_cmd/send_cmd pair that emits the END command (skipped when BTRFS_SEND_FLAG_OMIT_END_CMD is set). On success it returns 0 after the whole stream was written to the file for send_fd. In every post-increment case the cleanup frees the pending directory move, waiting directory move and orphan directory trees, drops send_in_progress (and the root reference where taken) of the clone roots taken so far (all of them including the send root once the clone roots were sorted, otherwise the first clone_sources_to_rollback ones and the send root counter) and of the parent root, frees clone_sources_tmp, releases the send file reference taken by fget (the caller's descriptor stays open), frees the clone roots array, send buffer, buffer pages, verity descriptor, caches, current inode state (iput) and the send context.
